sources: Times of Israel liveblog (Lazar Berman) + Al Jazeera report of the speech
fault_line: Is Netanyahu's 'end the Iranian threat once and for all' line a mandate from the election, or a caretaker leader using a war promise to hold power while 7 seats short of a majority?

sections.what_happened: In his first post-election speech at Likud headquarters in Jerusalem, Netanyahu said 'Iran is weaker than ever, Israel is stronger than ever,' said Israel with Trump has a 'historical opportunity' to 'remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all,' claimed the right-wing bloc won a 'decisive majority' among the Jewish/Zionist public, called for a 'strong, right-wing national government,' said a government relying on Arab parties must not be formed, and said 'we are still waiting for the true results' / final results in one or two days. He did not declare victory outright. Eisenkot, speaking in Tel Aviv, said voters delivered a vote of no confidence and urged Netanyahu to retire, warning him not to use Israel's security for political needs.
sections.what_verified: Two declared families carry the speech with identical wording: Times of Israel (T3) liveblog and Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA). Indian Express carries the same speech but has no declared tier in the registry and is not counted.
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu's 'decisive majority' claim conflicts with the count itself: at 66.2% counted his bloc held 56 seats, 5 short of 61 (1200-06), and exit polls put both main blocs near 51. His claim was explicitly limited to 'among the Zionist/Jewish public,' excluding Arab parties' seats. Eisenkot's rival claim (vote of no confidence) is a political claim, not a count result.
sections.why_matters: Before the count was finished, Netanyahu already named the next war's target: Iran, 'once and for all,' with Trump. The catch -- the count he was celebrating leaves him short of a majority.
sections.context: Background: BIG MISSED (not in any prior Oct 28 scan) -- Netanyahu election-night speech: 'Iran is weaker than ever; Israel is stronger than ever,' vows to end Iranian threat with Trump

totw_analysis: Our read: Before the count was finished, Netanyahu already named the next war's target: Iran, 'once and for all,' with Trump. The catch -- the count he was celebrating leaves him short of a majority. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Netanyahu's 'end the Iranian threat once and for all' line a mandate from the election, or a caretaker leader using a war promise to hold power while 7 seats short of a majority?
